**History of Life and Death.** **227**

<margin>04</margin> let us inquire; for the proper
work of cold is *Condensation*; and
it is perfected without any
malignancy, or inimical quality:
and therefore the operation is safer,
than by *Opiates*; although a little
less potent, if it were used only by turns,
as *Opiates* are: But again, because it
can be applied familiarly, and in the daily
diet moderately, it is also
by far more potent for the prolongati-
on of life, than by *Opiates*.

<margin>39</margin> *Refrigeration of the Spirits*, is done in three
ways; Either by *Respiration*;
Or by *Vapors*; Or by *Alimen-
ts*: The first is the best, but almost
outside our power; The second is
also potent, and yet is at hand;
The third is weak and through circuits.

*Air*

<summary>Bacon argues that the cooling of the vital spirits is a safer method for prolonging life than the use of opiates, as cold can be applied through diet daily without negative side effects. He briefly outlines three methods of refrigeration: respiration, vapors, and foods.</summary>
<keywords>refrigeration, vital spirits, condensation, respiration, vapors, food, longevity, Francis Bacon</keywords>
